title: Safe speed depends on the circumstances
summary: Traffic, manoeuvrability, visibility and environmental limits must be weighed together.
conditions: Safe speed is contextual rather than a universal number.
The vessel must retain scope for proper and effective action.

events.text: Safe speed is contextual rather than a universal number.

assumptions: Positions, timings, angles and separation are illustrative teaching choices, not rule-defined thresholds.
Motion is simplified and does not model hydrodynamics, stopping distance, current or sea state.
Vessel models and displayed lengths are scaled for legibility while preserving clearance between hulls.
Apply the COLREGs to the full circumstances; this scene is not an unconditional manoeuvring prescription.

sources.title: International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea — supplied course PDF

steps.title: Identify the conditions
steps.body: Safe speed is contextual rather than a universal number. The vessel must retain scope for proper and effective action.

steps.title: Apply the rule
steps.body: Traffic, manoeuvrability, visibility and environmental limits must be weighed together.

steps.title: Check the outcome
steps.body: Continue to assess the other vessel and the effect of any action until the vessels are finally past and clear.
